verses.text: On that day the LORD will punish Leviathan, the gliding serpent, Leviathan, the twisting serpent, with his fierce, great, and powerful sword. He will kill the dragon of the sea.
On that day, sing about a fruitful vineyard:
"I, the LORD, take care of it. I water it all the time. I guard it day and night so that no one can harm it.
I am not angry anymore. But if I find briers and thorns, I will go to battle against them. I will march out and burn them all up together.
Or else let them come to me for safety. Let them make peace with me. Yes, let them make peace with me."
In the days to come Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.
Has the LORD struck Israel as hard as he struck those who struck Israel? Has Israel been killed like those who killed them?
No, he punished them by sending them away into exile. He drove them out with his fierce wind, like the east wind.

In this way Jacob's guilt will be forgiven, and this is how his sin will be taken away: he will crush all the stones of the pagan altars like chalk, so that no Asherah poles or incense altars will be left standing.
The strong city is deserted, an empty place left behind like the wilderness. Calves feed there and lie down there. They strip its branches bare.

When its branches dry up, they are broken off, and women come and use them to make fires. For these are people without understanding. So the one who made them will not have pity on them. The one who formed them will show them no kindness.
On that day the LORD will thresh like a farmer, from the Euphrates River to the brook of Egypt. And you, people of Israel, will be gathered up one by one.

On that day a great trumpet will sound. Those who were dying in the land of Assyria, and those who were driven out to the land of Egypt, will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
